well: DSDP Hole 69-504B (Costa Rica Rift flank; 1.2272 N, -83.7302 E; seafloor -3,460 m) - SITE 504B, the same hole as entry 18's borehole fluids: the deepest hole in oceanic crust, here at its BIRTH (Leg 69 drilled the first 489 m in 1979)
operator_on_log: DSDP Leg 69, GLOMAR CHALLENGER (1979) - the catalogue's first Glomar Challenger data; shipboard density-porosity measurements on recovered basalt core; dataset Cann, White & Langseth via the DSDP/NGDC archive
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.221630 ('Physical properties of Hole 69-504B'); from the DSDP CD-ROM archive (NGDC/NOAA 1989); related to Init. Repts. DSDP 69 (doi:10.2973/dsdp.proc.69.1983)

coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 61 basalt core samples, 281.12 -> 484.06 mbsf (the upper pillow-basalt section of 504B as first drilled): water content, POROSITY (2.66-11.39 vol%), wet-bulk density (2.73-2.95 g/cm3), grain density (2.94-3.03 g/cm3), with per-sample DSDP core labels.
science_disclosure: THE SELF-AUDITING DATASET: porosity, grain density and bulk density are linked by the identity WBD = phi*rho_w + (1-phi)*rho_grain. The file carries all three, so the gate verifies the dataset against its own physics on all 61 rows (mean absolute closure ~0.01 g/cm3 at seawater rho_w = 1.025) - a 1979 laboratory's internal consistency, re-audited on every gate run. The porosity-depth structure (fresh massive units at ~2.7% vs altered/brecciated horizons at 10-11%) is the young-crust alteration story in numbers.
purpose: twenty-second catalogue entry - FIFTEENTH kind (physical properties: porosity/density family) and the catalogue's FIRST DSDP-ERA entry (Glomar Challenger, 1979 - scientific ocean drilling's founding vessel). Hole 504B becomes the catalogue's third multi-dataset family (entry 18 fluids at >160C ambient + entry 22 physical properties of the same rock those fluids react with).
verified: 61 samples; depth/porosity/density endpoints and extremes; the WBD identity closure computed live across all rows; per-sample labels; in-file license/coordinates to meta; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
